title: Modales de obligación y consejo (must, have to, should)
goal: Al terminar podrás explicar reglas de seguridad y requisitos, separar lo prohibido de lo opcional (mustn't vs don't have to), dar consejos y advertencias con la fuerza justa y hablar de obligaciones pasadas y futuras (had to, will have to) sin errores de forma.

lesson.title: ¿Qué es un verbo modal?
lesson.html:
En español casi todo se resuelve con deber, tener que y hay que. El inglés es más preciso: antes de hablar, el nativo decide cuánta fuerza tiene lo que dice (¿es un consejo, una advertencia o una obligación?) y de dónde viene (¿de su opinión, de una norma escrita, de la situación?). Elegir mal no suele ser un error gramatical, sino un error de mensaje: un you must a un colega puede sonar a orden, y un you should en una regla de seguridad suena a que es opcional.

Must y should son verbos modales: no expresan una acción, sino la actitud del hablante ante la acción. Tienen cuatro rasgos fijos que debes respetar siempre:

  • Una sola forma para todos: I must, he must. Nunca he musts.
  • Verbo base sin to después: You should call him. Nunca should to call.
  • Sin do/does/did: se niegan y se preguntan solos: shouldn't, Should I…?
  • Sin pasado ni futuro propios: no existe musted ni will must.

Have to y need to no son modales: son verbos normales que significan obligación. Por eso se conjugan (has to, had to, will have to) y usan do/does/did en negativo y pregunta, igual que en el Módulo 3. Esa diferencia es la clave de todo el módulo.

lesson.title: Las formas: must, have to y should
lesson.html:
MUST (modal)HAVE TO (verbo normal)SHOULD (modal)
AfirmativoI / He must go.I have to go. / He has to go.I / He should go.
NegativoYou mustn't go.
= prohibido		You don't have to go. / He doesn't have to go.
= no es necesario		You shouldn't go.
= no es buena idea
PreguntaMust I go?
(formal y poco usada)		Do I have to go? / Does he have to go?Should I go?
Respuesta cortaYes, you must. / No, you don't have to.Yes, you do. / No, you don't.Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.
Pasadohad tohad toshould have + participio (Módulo 19)
Futurowill have towill have toshould (sirve para futuro: You should go tomorrow.)

Regla de oro 1 — Modal + verbo base, sin TO y sin -S

Después de must, should va el verbo puro: She must sign. He should check. Nunca She must to sign ni He shoulds check.

Las expresiones have to, need to, ought to sí llevan to, porque el to es parte de la expresión, no un añadido.

Regla de oro 2 — MUSTN'T ≠ DON'T HAVE TO

En afirmativo, must y have to casi son sinónimos. En negativo se separan por completo: mustn't = está prohibido; don't have to = no es necesario, tú decides. Confundirlos es el error n.º 1 de los hispanohablantes, porque "no tienes que" y "no debes" se sienten parecidos en español.

lesson.title: MUST solo vive en el presente
lesson.html:
Regla de oro 3 — MUST solo vive en el presente

Para pasado y futuro, cambia a have to: I had to wait. We'll have to wait. Nunca I musted ni we will must: dos modales no pueden ir juntos.

Así piensa un nativo — must suena a reglamento

En el inglés hablado de EE. UU., la obligación diaria se dice casi siempre con have to o, de forma informal, I've got to go aiv GÓ-tə GOU. Must aparece sobre todo en textos escritos (carteles, manuales, contratos, procedimientos: All personnel must wear PPE.), en órdenes muy firmes y en recomendaciones entusiastas: You must try the ceviche!

Should es la herramienta de la cortesía: suaviza instrucciones entre colegas (You should check the gasket first.) y sirve para pedir opinión (Should I call the client?). Con un jefe o cliente, I think you should… suena profesional; You must… puede sonar a que le das órdenes.

lesson.title: Traducción directa vs interpretación real
lesson.html:
El verbo deber del español cubre tres ideas que en inglés son palabras distintas: obligación (must / have to), consejo (should) y deuda (owe). Además, hay que no tiene equivalente literal: el inglés necesita un sujeto (you, we).

Lo que piensas en españolLo que dice un nativo
Hay que firmar aquí.You have to sign here. There is to sign
No tienes que venir.You don't have to come. You mustn't come
No debes tocar eso.You mustn't touch that.
Deberías descansar.You should rest. You would should
Tuve que esperar.I had to wait. I musted wait
Le debo 20 dólares.I owe him 20 dollars. I must him
EspañolTraducción literal (mal)Inglés real
Debes usar casco.You must to use helmet.You have to wear a hard hat.
¿Debo llamarlo?Do I must call him?Should I call him?
Mejor te apuras.Better you hurry.You'd better hurry.
Tendré que trabajar el sábado.I will must work on Saturday.I'll have to work on Saturday.
Es obligatorio llevar arnés.Is obligatory to carry harness.You must wear a harness. / A harness is mandatory.
No es necesario que traigas nada.Is not necessary that you bring nothing.You don't need to bring anything.

Detalle léxico: la ropa y el equipo de protección se "llevan puestos" → wear, no use ni carry.

lesson.title: Detalles finos y mapa de decisión
lesson.html:
Detalles finos: had better, ought to, need to, be supposed to

  • had better (casi siempre 'd better): advertencia con consecuencia implícita, más urgente que should. Aunque tiene had, habla del presente o futuro: You'd better leave now (or you'll miss the bus). Negativo: You'd better not…, nunca You hadn't better.
  • ought to Ó-tə = should, un poco más formal. Se usa poco en preguntas y negativos; ahí prefiere should.
  • need to funciona como have to: Do I need to…? / You don't need to…. Es la forma más neutra para hablar de requisitos.
  • be supposed to = "se supone que debo": regla o expectativa que a veces no se cumple. I'm supposed to start at 7, but the gate is closed.
  • Con must también se hacen deducciones (He must be tired = debe de estar cansado). Eso se ve en el Módulo 17.

examples.en: All visitors must wear a hard hat and safety boots.
examples.es: Todos los visitantes deben usar casco y botas de seguridad.

examples.en: You mustn't start hot work without a signed permit.
examples.es: No debes empezar trabajos en caliente sin un permiso firmado.

examples.en: The welders have to finish the root pass before lunch.
examples.es: Los soldadores tienen que terminar el pase de raíz antes del almuerzo.

examples.en: The inspector has to check every weld on line 4.
examples.es: El inspector tiene que revisar cada soldadura de la línea 4.

examples.en: You don't have to print the drawings. The PDF is fine.
examples.es: No tienes que imprimir los planos. El PDF está bien.

examples.en: We need to send the quote by Friday.
examples.es: Tenemos que enviar la cotización a más tardar el viernes.

examples.en: You should ask Mark. He's worked on this type of tank before.
examples.es: Deberías preguntarle a Mark. Él ya ha trabajado en este tipo de tanque.

examples.en: You should drink more water and rest for three days.
examples.es: Debería tomar más agua y descansar tres días.

examples.en: Do I have to bring my passport to open an account?

examples.en: We had to wait four hours at the airport because of the storm.
examples.es: Tuvimos que esperar cuatro horas en el aeropuerto por la tormenta.

examples.en: We'd better confirm the price before we sign the contract.
examples.es: Más vale que confirmemos el precio antes de firmar el contrato.

examples.en: You must try the ceviche here. It's amazing!
examples.es: Tienes que probar el ceviche de aquí. ¡Es buenísimo!

examples.en: You don't have to bring anything. Just come!

examples.en: Next month we'll have to work on Saturdays to finish on time.

examples.en: Contractors must submit their safety plan before mobilization.
examples.es: Los contratistas deben presentar su plan de seguridad antes de la movilización.

dialog.text: Before you go in, there are a few rules. You must sign in at the gate every morning.
OK. Do I have to bring my own boots, or does the company provide them?
The company provides boots and a hard hat, so you don't have to buy anything.
Great. What about the tank? Can I go inside today?
Not yet. You mustn't enter the tank without a confined space permit. Mr. Lee has to sign it first.
Understood. How long does it take to get the permit?
Usually about an hour. You should ask for it early, around 6:30.
Got it. Is there anything else I need to know?
Yes. It gets really hot after 11, so you'd better drink a lot of water.
Good advice. Yesterday I had to stop early because of the heat.
And one more thing: you don't have to call me "ma'am." Sarah is fine!

errors.wrong: You must to wear a helmet.
errors.right: You must wear a hard hat.
errors.why: Modal + verbo base, sin to. En obra se dice hard hat.
Los modales no llevan -s en tercera persona.
Have to es verbo normal: he/she/it → has to.

errors.wrong: You mustn't come tomorrow. (= no es necesario)
errors.right: You don't have to come tomorrow.
errors.why: Mustn't prohíbe; lo opcional es don't have to.
Must no tiene pasado: se usa had to.
Must no usa do; con do va have to.
Con does el verbo vuelve a la forma base: have.

errors.wrong: I will must work on Sunday.
errors.right: I'll have to work on Sunday.
errors.why: Dos modales no se combinan: will have to.
Should se niega solo: should not / shouldn't.

falseFriends.means: Deuda = owe; must es solo obligación.
Advice (sustantivo) es incontable. El verbo es advise əd-VÁIZ.
falseFriends.fix: some advice / a piece of advice

falseFriends.en: I recommend you to check it.
falseFriends.means: Recommend no va con persona + to (Módulo 22).
falseFriends.fix: I recommend checking it. / You should check it.

falseFriends.means: En documentos técnicos se usa mandatory o required.
Obligate es legal y formal; en el habla: make + persona + verbo.
falseFriends.fix: They made us stay. / We had to stay.

answers: You should talk to the supervisor.

answers: Do I have to bring my passport?

A1.prompt: Ayer tuvimos que trabajar hasta las 9.
answers: Yesterday we had to work until 9.
We had to work until 9 yesterday.
Yesterday we had to work until nine.
A1.explain: Pasado de la obligación → had to. Until 9 = hasta las 9.

A1.prompt: Ella tiene que terminar los planos hoy.
answers: She has to finish the drawings today.
A1.explain: Tercera persona → has to. Planos = drawings.

A1.prompt: Más vale que nos vayamos ya; está lloviendo mucho.
answers: We'd better leave now; it's raining hard.
We'd better leave now; it is raining hard.
We had better leave now; it's raining hard.
We had better leave now; it is raining hard.

We'd better leave now. It's raining hard.

A1.explain: Advertencia con consecuencia → 'd better + verbo base. También it's raining a lot.

answers: What should I do?
A1.explain: Pedir consejo → WH- + should + sujeto + verbo.

A1.prompt: El próximo mes tendremos que cambiar las válvulas.
answers: Next month we'll have to change the valves.
Next month we will have to change the valves.
Next month we'll have to replace the valves.
Next month we will have to replace the valves.
We'll have to change the valves next month.
We will have to change the valves next month.

A2.prompt: You don't need to come early tomorrow.

A2.prompt: We had to cancel the meeting because the client was sick.
answers: Tuvimos que cancelar la reunión porque el cliente estaba enfermo.
Tuvimos que cancelar la reunión porque el cliente se enfermó.
A2.explain: Had to = tuvimos que (pasado de obligación).

A2.prompt: You're not supposed to use your phone in the control room.

Look at that sign: "All personnel [1] wear PPE." No exceptions.
OK. Can I take photos of the tanks for my report?
No. You [2] take photos without permission. It's a client rule.
Understood. Do I [3] attend the safety meeting every morning?
Yes. But Mr. Lee is the manager, so he [4] attend. He comes when he can.
Next month there's a shutdown, so we [5] work on Saturdays.
No problem. At my last job I [6] work every Sunday!
Great attitude. It's very hot at noon. My advice: you [7] drink water every hour.
Yes. It's 6:40 and the meeting starts at 6:45. You [8] hurry, or you'll be late!

C2.prompt: Redacta un correo. Escribe un correo de 6 a 8 oraciones a una persona nueva en tu equipo sobre las reglas de la obra. Incluye: (a) saludo y propósito, (b) dos obligaciones con must o have to, (c) una prohibición con mustn't, (d) algo no necesario con don't have to, (e) un consejo con should, (f) una advertencia con 'd better o una obligación pasada con had to, (g) despedida profesional.
C2.model:
Subject: Welcome to the T-205 project
Hi Ana,
Welcome to the team! Here are a few site rules before you start on Monday. You have to sign in at the gate every morning, and you must wear your hard hat and safety boots at all times. You mustn't enter the tank without a confined space permit. You don't have to bring any tools, because the company provides everything. You should arrive a little early on your first day, since the safety induction takes about an hour. Last week a new welder had to wait two hours because he forgot his ID, so you'd better bring yours.
Best regards,
Edwin
